verdict.rationale: Jitsu Functions are JavaScript/TypeScript code that runs on every incoming event before delivery. They can filter, transform or enrich the event, and their Fetch API can call third-party services, so code-defined logic can fire actions per event. A webhook destination can also forward events to any HTTP endpoint. This is a data-processing pipeline rather than a dedicated rules or automation engine, so automation depth is only implied. missing for 10: a declarative rule/trigger builder, documented event-to-action automation workflows (conditional actions beyond filter/transform), examples of action-triggering use cases, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Functions are designed to process data in Jitsu before it is sent to the destination... Filter... Transform... Enrich
Fetch API - Perform HTTP requests to third-party services.
Send data to any HTTP endpoint. You can use this destination to send data to Slack, Discord, or any other service that accepts HTTP requests.
Filter - Exclude data that fails to meet your specified criteria.
